messages.subject: Sigma not positive definite...
parts:
This is the error I get when trying to calculate the posterior for my model.
There is also a warning from precis(the model) that states: In sqrt(diag(vcov(model))) : NaNs produced. I can see this in the output as:
          Estimate  Std. Error         2.5%        97.5%
a      0.053209054 0.019704143  0.014589644  0.091828464
bt     0.079442445 0.018737890  0.042716856  0.116168034

bps    0.012440669 0.002025419  0.008470921  0.016410418
bstp   0.007916405         NaN          NaN          NaN
sigma  0.047326232 0.001430249  0.044522996  0.05012946


I need the interaction effect of the variable "s" with "t" and "p", so I need a way to do this.
I'm using Richard McElreath's rethinking package and the function mle2() to create my models.

Any ideas?

Much appreciated!

Iara

messages.author: 8d1674b7b16af1b1
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Sigma not positive definite...
parts:
Both the error message and the warning indicate that mle2 is having trouble figuring out the amount of uncertainty associated with some of the parameter estimates.  It's hard to know why that might be, but I have a couple of questions that might lead to some more information:

1) Is there any indication that mle2 hasn't fully converged?

2) What happens if you just do `vcov(model)`?

3) If you multiplied data$s * data$t * data$p together, are the numbers very close to 0 or 10^16? Maybe R is getting numerical issues.  If that's what's going on, you can just rescale one or more of them by changing the units (e.g. from meters to millimeters or whatever).

Hope one of these is helpful!

Dave
